variables.label: Min. unit size

variables.cite: current zoning regs — not located; flagged version discrepancy

variables.district: Town-wide (≥5 net new units) / 15% in TOD areas & DRD overlay
variables.label: Inclusionary zoning
variables.value: 12% of units must be set aside as Below Market Rate (BMR); 15% in Commerce Drive/TOD/DRD/Transit-Oriented Downtown
variables.quote: Any project that results in a net increase of 5 or more dwelling units, whether by new construction or by the alteration, expansion, reconstruction, or change of existing residential or nonresidential space shall include provision to set aside not less than 12% of said units as below market rate (BMR) units.

variables.label: Historic overlay
variables.value: Reviewed by Fairfield HDC; case law confirms review scope limited to changes visible from a public way
variables.cite: CGS §7-147a et seq.; Gibbons v. Fairfield HDC, 285 Conn. 755 (2008)

variables.label: Demolition delay
variables.value: 10 days for structures <100 years old; 60 days for structures ≥100 years old

source.title: Fairfield Code of Ordinances, Ch. 57 (Demolition, adopted 2007) — exact URL not captured during research

variables.cite: §57-2C/D (not independently re-verified — lives in the Code of Ordinances, not the zoning regulations PDF)

variables.district: Coastal Site Plan Review, Section 34 (true coastal town)
variables.label: Coastal/flood overlay
variables.value: Applies — Long Island Sound frontage; FEMA Zones A/AE/VE, Zone VE also a Coastal High Hazard Area
variables.quote: All buildings, uses and structures fully or partially within the coastal boundary as defined by Section 22a-94 of the Connecticut General Statutes and as delineated on the Coastal Boundary Map for the Town of Fairfield, shall be subject to the coastal site plan review requirements and procedures in Sections 22a-105 through 22a-109 of the Connecticut General Statutes.

hap_score.methodology_note: Computed from the Variables table on this page, not from the NZA data below. Six weighted components (Multifamily Access 30pts, Approval Discretion 10pts, Minimum Lot Size 20pts, ADU Approval Pathway 15pts, Parking Mandate 10pts, Demolition Delay 15pts) are each scored against a fixed, published rubric from a specific cited fact above. Higher = more restrictive.

v2.formula: V2 = sum(district score x acres) / sum(acres) over included districts
v2.method: Each district is scored with the same six-component rubric using only its own rules. The score uses four components that every town can document (multifamily access, approval discretion, minimum lot size, ADU pathway); a district is included only if all four are confirmed. Parking and demolition delay are shown as context but not scored, so towns share one scale. The town V2 score is the land-area-weighted mean of included district scores; acreage is from data/land_area/fairfield.json. Components with no confirmed input are excluded per district.
